Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

engage verb

join battle

also join battle, engage the enemy, come to blows, start a fight

classical

Caes. BG 2.21: proeliī committendī signum dare (Lewis & Short)
Nep. Eum. 3: in aciem exercitum ēdūxit proeliumque commīsit (Lewis & Short)

proelium committere

phrase: <span lang="la">committō, committere, commīsī, commissum</span> with <span lang="la">proelium</span> (or <span lang="la">pugnam, certāmen</span>)

join battle, begin a fight

Committere on its own is “bring together, join”, and also “entrust” and “commit (a crime)” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • manum (manūs) cōnserere — come to close quarters, come to blows

    phrase: <span lang="la">cōnserō, cōnserere, cōnseruī, cōnsertum</span> with <span lang="la">manum</span>, <span lang="la">cum</span> and the ablative or <span lang="la">inter sē</span> · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 20: signa contulit, manum cōnseruit, magnās cōpiās hostium fūdit (Lewis & Short); Liv. 7.40.14: manūs inter sē (Lewis & Short)

    Hand-to-hand fighting; cōnserere alone is “join, fasten together”, and with proelium or pugnam it is the same as committere (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • signa contulit, manum cōnseruit, magnās cōpiās hostium fūdit

    he joined battle, came to close quarters and routed great forces of the enemyCic. Mur. 20 (Lewis & Short)

  • in aciem exercitum ēdūxit proeliumque commīsit

    he led his army out into line and engagedNep. Eum. 3 (Lewis & Short)

  • Puerī inter sē manūs cōnseruērunt.

    The boys came to blows.composed

See also battle, attack, be involved.

SourcesLewis & Short: committo · Lewis & Short: consero · Lewis & Short: proelium
